evidence: books/served-catalog.lisp:1579-1583 (fn-nntp-listgroup-result-cat): `(shown (fn-scat-range-numbers group (nfix (fn-nntp-range-low range)) (nfix (fn-nntp-range-high range)) v fn-cat)) ... (fn-nntp-multi-octets next-session ... (fn-nntp-number-lines shown))`, where LISTGROUP with no range uses all-range (1 2147483647). The same holds at books/served-catalog.lisp:1879-1885 (fn-nntp-hdr-command-cat range arm: fn-scat-range-numbers then fn-nntp-hdr-lines-for-numbers-cat, then fn-nntp-multi) and at :2028-2035 (fn-nntp-xpat-response-cat: the full range, a wildmat match per article, one fn-nntp-multi). By contrast, OVER uses fn-ovw-start/fn-ovw-cursor-effect so that 'the step's work' does not grow with the range (comment at :746-776). The fn-scat-range-numbers definition at :596-598 has no window.
fix: Give LISTGROUP, the HDR/XHDR range form and the XPAT range form the same treatment as OVER: return a cursor effect from an O(1) start and drain at most W numbers per quantum (generalize fn-ovw-cursor over a line renderer). Add the expand-to-unbounded keystone that fn-nntp-over-range-ovw already has.
reviewer: fn-nntp-listgroup-result-cat (books/served-catalog.lisp:1572-1585) calls fn-scat-range-numbers over the whole range and emits one multi-line reply. The HDR/XHDR range arm (:1876-1885) and XPAT (:2027-2035) do the same. Only OVER/XOVER uses the fn-ovw cursor (:746-776). books/served.lisp:3089-3114 itself records as OPEN that one step's cost is unbounded and names LISTGROUP over a range as the worst case. The work is clamped to the group high, so it grows with the group's size, not with 2^31, but it still runs whole in one step under the owner gate, which breaks D27.
scenario: Any reader on a group with N articles sends 'LISTGROUP big.group' or 'XHDR Subject 1-' (slrn and tin send XHDR), or 'XPAT Subject 1- *x*'. A single served step probes every number, reads every header through the arena, builds N reply lines and appends them into one reply octet list. The owner runs this under its gate, so for N in the millions it blocks every other connection for the duration and allocates O(total header bytes) at once. That violates D27 ('bound work and allocation per scheduling step') exactly as OVER did before PRF-1020. The pipelined variants make it worse.
title: LISTGROUP, HDR/XHDR range and XPAT range are answered whole in one served step (only OVER/XOVER got the windowed cursor)
